subject: Intermittent on‑prem service timeouts after private cutover — DNS masquerade + MSS symptoms
messages:
From: Marisol Vega <ops@mercury-health.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Perez <alex.perez@mercury-health.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent internal service timeouts after private cutover

Hi Logan,

We started our private deployment cutover to the Redwood Private plane late last night (per the cutover checklist). Since ~03:30 UTC we're seeing intermittent timeouts and failed uploads from our on‑prem ingestion service to the hosted inference endpoints. Symptoms:

- Large payload uploads (multi‑MB) often stall and then retry, sometimes generating 504/timeout at the app layer.
- Smaller requests succeed.
- TCP retransmits visible in our capture; occasional ICMP 'fragmentation needed' messages seen in traceroutes.
- DNS lookups from the ingestion host are intermittently resolving to the wrong resolver (we see queries hitting an external resolver IP).

We've attached a short traceroute and a packet capture (packet_capture_fragment.pcap) for the window 03:28–03:40 UTC. We've also included a brief list of our steps (mercury_traceroute_0708.txt).

Can Redwood ops triage? Priority: high — this is impacting nightly batch processing. If it's MTU, NAT, or SG related, we need guidance and a rollback plan.

Thanks,
Marisol Vega
NetOps Lead — Mercury Health
ops@mercury-health.com

Attachments: packet_capture_fragment.pcap, mercury_traceroute_0708.txt

Initial read: the combination of ICMP 'fragmentation needed' and large‑payload stalls points at a PMTU / MSS clamp issue somewhere in the path. The DNS queries being rewritten to an external resolver is concerning — that can cause odd connection attempts and additional latency.

Actionable next steps from our side:
- I'll start a quick conntrack & NAT port churn analysis against the packet capture.
- Stephanie, can you run a control tcpdump from our private gateway (<redacted‑gateway‑ip>) during the window Marisol sent?
- Mina, please check any expected iptables prerouting/mangle rules on the on‑prem gateway for masquerade of UDP/53.

Marisol — can you confirm whether there was any firewall update or transparent proxy change applied at cutover? Also, do you have a maintenance window tonight (UTC) where we can schedule an active test?

I'll follow up with a short triage note within the hour.

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marisol Vega <ops@mercury-health.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 11:22:37 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent internal service timeouts after private cutover

On Tue, Jul 11, 2028 at 10:23 AM Marisol Vega <ops@mercury-health.com> wrote:
> We started our private deployment cutover to the Redwood Private plane late last night ...

Quick notes from the packet capture and traceroute:

- Packet sample shows TCP MSS advertised 1460 from the client, but we see outgoing packets with 1500 payloads being dropped; ICMP 'frag needed' originates from the customer's edge firewall (next‑hop). That matches a PMTU blackhole.
- The path shows an asymmetric routing event for some flows — two of the three ECMP nexthops are rewriting src ports (SNAT) differently, causing conntrack to create duplicate entries and rapid ephemeral port churn. We can see SYN retransmits and short NAT timeouts leading to RSTs when the server's response returns via another path.
- DNS traffic: there's a PREROUTING MASQUERADE rule on the customer's gateway that rewrites 53/udp to the external resolver IP; during bursts some queries end up at the wrong resolver and get rate‑limited.

Recommended immediate actions (can be executed in a 30‑m maintenance window):
1) Apply an MSS clamp on the customer firewall's egress chain to 1380 (covers overhead for tunnels). Example iptables rule: iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
2) Remove the MASQUERADE rule that targets UDP/53 in PREROUTING so internal DNS resolves use the internal resolver. We'll provide the exact match condition (see attached recommended_config_snippet.txt).
3) Expand the SNAT ephemeral pool temporarily to reduce port exhaustion while we stabilize.
4) Add a temporary static route for the inference endpoint subnet to prefer the low‑latency ECMP path (pinning) while we validate conntrack stability.

If steps 1–3 are applied together they should remove the ICMP frag errors and reduce retries. I'll stand by to validate captures in real time.

— Stephanie
Senior Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com

Attachment: recommended_config_snippet.txt

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Marisol Vega <ops@mercury-health.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 21:05:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent internal service timeouts after private cutover

Following up with the iptables diff we found on the on‑prem gateway. I pulled the candidate ruleset and compared it to the pre‑cutover snapshot — the only new rule that lines up with the symptoms is a broad MASQUERADE for UDP that matches port 53 and translates it to an external resolver IP (likely a leftover from the migration playbook). That matches Marisol's symptom set.

I've prepared a minimal patch (iptables-diff.patch) that:
- removes the single MASQUERADE rule matching udp dport 53 in PREROUTING, and
- inserts an explicit ACCEPT for src subnet X.X.X.0/24 to the internal resolver IP before any NAT rules, and
- adds a short‑term logging rule so we can confirm no queries get misrouted post‑rollback.

Recommended rollback plan (low risk):
1) Put the edge firewall in maintenance mode for 20 minutes.
2) Apply the iptables patch.
3) Apply the MSS clamp in the FORWARD chain as Stephanie suggested.
4) Monitor application logs and tcpdump for 2 maintenance windows (10 minutes each).

If the above clears the failures we'll then:
- revert the SNAT expansion after 24 hours if conntrack entries stabilize, and
- work with Mercury to harden the NAT ruleset so DNS is never subject to masquerade.

— Mina
Network SRE, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

Attachment: iptables-diff.patch
